scope: Retire the post-NGE current/lifetime GCW point, PvP-kill rating-input, weekly rating conversion, decay, invasion-credit, rating-derived regional-score progression, passive combat-level/rank factional-presence writer, manual/admin and native regional-score writers and decay, false holiday point rewards, destructive point-consumable interactions, NGE percentile overwrite of planetary control, regional-score travel/spawn/space-battle gameplay authority, later city/guild regional-defender membership, bonus, title, and presentation, the later fixed-base/Restuss PvP-region bonus controller, and the post-NGE civilian neutral factional-helper/mercenary status while restoring Publish 14 player-base control scores and registry lifecycle, real faction enlistment and on-leave/covert/overt transitions, faction standing/rank, ordinary open-world PvP, the Yavin IV Force Ranking System and Jedi enclaves, ambient encounter availability, general regional presentation compatibility, and independent mission, quest, PRE-CU open-world battlefield, holiday-token, and space rewards.

findings: Publish 14 uses faction standing and the independently persisted creature faction rank; the pinned Publish 14 reference does not contain the later current/lifetime GCW point or weekly rating/decay progression system.
Publish 14 planetary control is recomputed from registered player faction bases using exact authored HQ values: s01 1/2, s02 3/6, s03 4/8, and s04 10/20 for PvE/PvP variants.

The ten hard-coded gcw_master_objects object IDs in the later source are absent from current buildouts and the durable live object set; the always-present planet object is therefore the authoritative home for PRE-CU control state and its hourly base-registry reconciliation.

The cluster-wide faction-base registry is the absolute reconciliation source, so a destroyed base must remove its own registry element before applying the immediate score/count decrement; otherwise the next hourly pass can resurrect the removed base's authority.

Legacy ratio and dictionary readers must resolve the planet-owned scores directly; copied child objvars remain presentation compatibility only and cannot be an independent or stale gameplay authority.

The pinned Publish 14 reference chooses the winning faction from raw base-score totals and advances NPC difficulty when the winning score delta reaches the authored 64-point threshold, rather than using the later regional percentile service.
The pinned recruiter omits s05 from its purchasable installation list and the pinned score map has no s05 entry; retained later s05 assets therefore have no PRE-CU planetary-control authority.
An exact search of pinned Core3 for gcw_region_defender, gcwregiondefender, GCW defender region, and war planner finds no city/guild regional-defender enrollment, reward bonus, or title subsystem.

An exact search of pinned Core3 for GCW score, GCWScore, ImperialScorePercentile, RebelScorePercentile, adjustGCW, and decayGCW finds no later regional raw-score, percentile, adjustment-queue, or weekly-decay subsystem.

The pinned Publish 14 reference contains no regional-control travel perk, officer starport restriction, regional travel surcharge, GCW-threshold ambient spawn filter, or regional-score space-battle side selector.

The retained open-world battlefield commands have no NGE level, expertise, profession-template, queue, or token gate; the direct battlefield scripts award 25 faction standing after more than ten percent participation only when a victory lasts at least 900 seconds.
The dormant battlefield_utility speech script has no production object-template or buildout attachment; its testing-only faction grant is not a player-reachable reward path.

The later ambient spawn tables retain 958 authored factional rows across 87 files as content metadata; removing the regional-score filter returns both factions to ordinary PRE-CU encounter selection rather than suppressing them at a frozen score.
The retained ground mission path awards credits and faction standing independently of its later GCW-rating side effect.
The retained space kill path already awards authored Rebel/Imperial faction standing, and the space battle path awards physical faction tokens independently of later GCW-rating points.

The pinned Publish 14 reference has faction standing and rank rather than the later consumable GCW-point currency; later holiday token content can remain, but it must not emit a false point-reward message or mutate the retired currency.

All fourteen authored later GCW-point collection items and their metadata remain available as content, while their destructive radial consume path is retired until an explicit PRE-CU reward conversion is designed.

The retained War Terminal is a later publish-gift asset whose planetary report and factional-presence presentation can remain, but its queued-battlefield action and 30-day personal-contribution ledger are consumers of systems retired elsewhere in this contract.
Persisted gcwContributionTracking state and cached terminal actions can outlive their writers, so they must be scrubbed rather than displayed as current PRE-CU progression.

Four later pvp_region_watcher objects remain in the Corellia, Talus, Naboo, and Restuss buildouts; their controller scripts record deaths and feed the retired NGE regional GCW-point bonus path, which is absent from the pinned Publish 14 reference.

The watcher scenery can remain as inert authored content, but its buildout scripts, planet registrations, cycle state, persisted player activity flag, death callback, and bonus callback must be unreachable while ordinary open-world PvP and PRE-CU battlefields remain intact.

The pinned Publish 14 reference explicitly enables the Force Ranking System, initializes it only when Yavin IV is running, persists both council rosters, configures rank rooms and maintenance, and uses the exact 12-rank experience matrix restored here.
Publish 14 Force Ranking members are aligned Light-to-Rebel or Dark-to-Imperial and remain overt; rank ownership is a skill predicate, not a script-attachment predicate.
A disabled Force Ranking configuration may make enclave cells public and stop maintenance, but must not erase persisted council rosters, voting state, cluster data, or rank membership.
The pinned Publish 14 recruiter changes an actually enlisted player's on-leave, covert, and overt faction status; it contains no civilian neutral-mercenary writer or factional-helper shortcut.
Later faction conversations and quests remain available, but a player must use the retained faction-enlistment path before receiving factional PvP status.
